title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(鹿田正昭研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Shikada Masaaki)
educationalGoal: Objectives of education for the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering.●Based on the educational objectives in the curriculum guidebook, we will practice specific themes centered on “Basic Abilities for Utilizing the Natural Environment”.● Actively participate to the “Spatial Information Project” in collaboration with Nonoichi City as a regional partner.
advice: Based on themes addressed at the Shikada Laboratory, this course will focus on regional information related to spatial information technology. The contents are as follows. ●Assignments will be given by teachers or selected from regional collaboration projects. If a student selects a regional cooperation project, a project plan must be prepared. ●Students practice themes that they devised in the Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III. ●Students will practice advanced research themes with graduate students on the premise of going on to graduate school.The basic schedule is as follows. Both terms’ topics are closely related to comprehensive learning (active learning).○ 7th term (first semester): Students review their basic knowledge of spatial information technology and read papers and journals, and make a presentation. They review the project considered in Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III, and read English papers, understanding the outline of their spatial information projects. They must actively participate in their projects.○8th term (second semester): Themes will be undertaken individually or in groups to address the specific content proposed in the previous semester. Based on progress reports, monthly reports, English papers, etc., students will self-assess the degree to which they achieve the aims of their themes. Students will actively participate in regional collaboration projects related to spatial information. Students’ time spent in this effort must exceed 450 hours between the two semesters. Times shown in the syllabus are the minimum required for preparation and review. Reference the e-syllabus for the latest information of class relating Covid-19
books: Textbooks:None Reference books:Ace Surveying [ASAKURA], Spatial Information Technology [Japan Survey Association] Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: Students should review previously studied materials such as Surveying I and II, Surveying Practicum/Exercise I and II, spatial information technology, Environmental Civil Engineering Experiments/Exercise III.[ They should review the textbooks and materials used in this course and be prepared for the Spatial Information Project. They should review the science seminar (Camelia Kids) learned in Surveying I.

achievementLevels.ideal: ・Students acquire a basic knowledge of geographic information systems (GIS) and can explain GIS application fields in detail. They can use program and used advanced GIS software. Students understand GNSS application fields in detail after acquiring basic GNSS knowledge. They can operate a GNSS receiver and analyze the data. ・They can explain R/S applications in detail after acquiring basic R/S knowledge. They can overlay many maps using GIS software. ・Students can contribute to society by participating in collaborative regional spatial information projects. Students can write project reports in English
achievementLevels.standard: ・Students acquire a basic knowledge of geographic information systems (GIS) and can explain the concept of GIS. They can operate GIS software. ・Students acquire a basic knowledge of global positioning systems (GNSS) and can explain the outline of GNSS. ・They also acquire basic knowledge about R/S and can explain its concepts. Students can explain collaborative applications of GNSS, GIS, and R/S. ・Students can read English papers. ・They can play an active role as a leader in community contributions (Camelia Kids). ・As per the outline of the PDIII Public Presentation Review Board, students must be able to write in English.
